Even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews. I work in insurance claims, you know, processing policies and stuff, and it's just... I don't know, I get up, and then I'm in the breakroom, and someone brought donuts the other day. Glazed ones, from that place on 4th street? They're so good, but they always run out of the chocolate frosted ones first. Anyway, my supervisor is starting to notice I'm not at my desk when I should be.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they keep getting up from their workstation during the day when they are expected to stay put and finish their work.

turns.doctor_question: When you're sitting at your desk trying to do your work, do you find it hard to keep your attention on the task itself, or is it more that you feel restless and need to get up and move around?
turns.patient_response: Um, I think it's more that my attention just... slides right off what I'm doing. Like, I'll be staring at a file, and if the people in the next cubicle start talking about another claim, or if I just suddenly remember some random errand I have to do after work... like picking up my dry cleaning. Actually, I need to find a new dry cleaner because the one I go to shrunk my favorite sweater last week. It was this really nice wool one my mom got me for Christmas, and now it could probably fit a toddler. It's such a hassle to find a place that actually reads the care labels, you know? But anyway, yeah, I'll get distracted by a thought like that, or my coworkers talking, and my focus is just gone. I end up having to reread the exact same section of the claim a few times before it actually registers in my brain.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes difficulty sustaining attention on their work, noting that their attention 'slides right off' and they have to reread sections multiple times.

I remember this one time in fourth grade, Mr. Henderson's class—he was obsessed with dinosaurs and had this huge T-Rex skull replica on his desk that we weren't allowed to touch. Which was honestly so unfair because why put it right there in front of us if we can't even touch it, right? He said it was fragile, but I'm pretty sure it was just cheap plastic. He bought it at a museum gift shop on a road trip, I think. I love road trips, actually, except for the fast food. You eat burgers for three days straight and you just feel terrible. 

But anyway, I'd always lose his spelling packets, or I'd just completely miss the instructions when he was explaining what we were supposed to do. My mom actually tried color-coding my folders to help me keep track of things. Red for math, blue for reading... I think green was science? Or maybe green was social studies. But yeah, my teachers always had to come over to my desk and give me constant reminders to actually finish my classwork instead of just sitting there. So I guess the missing instructions and needing someone to remind me to finish my work has kind of always been a thing.

It was a Dodge Caravan, one of those weird teal colors they used to make in the 90s. We called it the "Teal Turtle" because it was so incredibly slow going uphill. We took it on a road trip to the Grand Canyon once, and I swear I thought we were going to start rolling backward when we were driving up some of those mountain passes. My sister got carsick on that trip, actually. She always got carsick, even on short trips to the grocery store. She had to sit in the front seat with the window down, which meant I was stuck in the back with all the luggage and the cooler. The cooler was always packed with these little juice boxes that were impossible to open without squirting juice everywhere. 

But yeah, no, to answer your question, I've never been officially evaluated or diagnosed with anything before this. This is the first time I'm really looking into it.

I refuse to upgrade because I hate the idea of not having a real button to press. Plus, the new ones don't even come with a charger in the box anymore, which feels like a total scam. You pay a thousand dollars for a phone and they can't even give you a little plastic brick to plug it into the wall? It's ridiculous. 

But yeah, work is where the forgetting really gets me in trouble. The follow-ups and the forms and stuff. At home, I don't really have claimants waiting on me to send them things, so it's not as big of a deal.

He had all these exotic fish in there, like these bright blue ones that would dart around, and this one ugly bottom-feeder that just sucked on the glass all day. But yeah, to answer your question, no, nobody ever told me I couldn't sit still or that I moved around too much. It was just the spacing out and losing stuff.

But no, I wasn't interrupting or acting crazy. I was just in my own little world most of the time. The teachers mostly just said I needed to apply myself more, you know?
